newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended down on Tuesday as disappointment spurred by a poor June private sector credit extension data dashed hopes of an imminent interest rate cut.

Dealers said the credit data released late on Monday tarnished expectations that Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals would ease rates, despite better M3 figures, lower consumer inflation and a surge in the June trade surplus.

"I think people are not too happy with the economic data that's come through and that's why we are closing down. (The credit extension data) is saying the likelihood of a rate cut now is less," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said.
"But our view is still that the scope is still there for a cut in the last quarter of the year," the dealer added.
The industrials finished down 20.7 points at 9,105.3 as the all-shares slid off by 17.0 points to close at 7,473.8.
Dealers said Monday's late run had also fuelled some profit-taking on the industrials as gold which which started firmer on Tuesday slid back amid bullion's fall from day's highs.

Bullion, which closed above $328 per ounce on Monday with gold analysts in London saying the price suggested a breakout was being attempted and could lead to a test of $335.70 per ounce, was last bid at $326.30 an ounce.
The gold index closed off 4.3 points at 986.5.
Dealers said overall market volumes were moderate with around 700 million rand worth of shares changing hands during the day.
They added that Wednesday's trading could continue drifty as market players continued to digest the recent swathe of economic data for direction.
Some further profit-taking was also seen continuing to grip the industrials although the market's underlying sentiment remained upbeat.
"The CPI figure seems to have perked the market up a little and now I think it will probably recover on the back of the CPI and trade surplus figures," one dealer commented.
Among shares basking in the limelight were furniture group Profurn which finished four cents up at 238 cents as investors snap the shares in anticipation of good future earnings growth.

Volumes on Profurn were last around 5.5 million shares while on the gold board Kloof added 20 cents to 24.20 rand as Randgold shed 140 cents to 16.50 rand after second quarter gold mining earnings slides into loss.
Newly-listed base metals group Billiton closed down 80 cents at 16.40 rand as Monday's debut interest started to wane, dealers said.
As on the cash market, the South African industrial futures finished lower, knocked by profit-taking.
Some futures dealers, however, said the dip could prove temporary with many players viewing the jump in June credit extension as a once-off.
"Credit extension figures weren't good but I think the guys might be interpreting them as a once-off situation. It looks like a rate cut is not imminent but it's certainly on the horizon," one said.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,643/46 from the 8,666 settlement on Monday, the all-shares contract was at 6,710/20 from 6,739 and the golds contract at 693/99 from 694 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
